hints.title: Order Preservation Obstacle
hints.text: Scanning every item in linear time becomes too slow when queries repeat over massive ordered lists. Can you discard half of the candidates after checking the midpoint?

hints.title: Lower Bound Invariant
hints.text: Maintain a search window [left, right]. When target exceeds the midpoint value, the answer must lie strictly to the right; otherwise, it lies at or to the left.

hints.title: Bisection Procedure
hints.text: Initialize left to 0 and right to len(nums) - 1. While left is at most right, compute mid = left + (right - left) // 2. If nums[mid] is target, return mid. If nums[mid] < target, advance left = mid + 1; otherwise shrink right = mid - 1. At termination, left points to the correct insert index.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Logarithmic bisection discarding half of the search interval each step in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Linear scan takes O(N) comparisons which violates the required O(log N) runtime bound.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant auxiliary pointers eliminate unnecessary array allocations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Avoiding integer overflow when computing midpoint and handling left boundary convergence when target is absent.
